dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: ADHD medicines such as amphetamine (Adderall), methylphenidate (Ritalin) or lisdexamfetamine are strong stimulants, and even small amounts can seriously harm dogs: agitation, pacing, a racing heart, overheating and seizures. Call your vet immediately.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: ADHD medicines such as amphetamine (Adderall), methylphenidate (Ritalin) or lisdexamfetamine are strong stimulants, and even small amounts can seriously harm cats: agitation, pacing, a racing heart, overheating and seizures. Call your vet immediately.

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Alcohol poisons dogs. Beer, wine, spirits, alcohol-based hand sanitiser and fermenting bread dough can all cause it. Signs usually start within 30 to 60 minutes: vomiting, wobbliness and drowsiness, and in severe cases dangerously slow breathing, a low body temperature and coma.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Alcohol poisons cats too, from drinks, alcohol-based hand sanitiser or fermenting bread dough. Signs usually start within 30 to 60 minutes: vomiting, wobbliness and drowsiness, and in severe cases dangerously slow breathing, a low body temperature and coma.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicoses From Alcohols in Animals
Kovalkovičová et al., "Some food toxic for pets", Interdisciplinary Toxicology (2009)

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Onions, garlic, leeks and chives damage a dog's red blood cells and can cause anaemia, whether raw, cooked, dried or powdered. Signs usually appear a few days after eating them, once the damage is done, so call your vet even if your dog seems fine.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Cats are the most sensitive of all species to onions, garlic, leeks and chives: even a small amount of cooked onion has poisoned cats. They damage red blood cells and cause anaemia, with signs usually appearing a few days later, so call your vet even if your cat seems fine.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Garlic and Onion (Allium spp) Toxicosis in Animals
Kovalkovičová et al., "Some food toxic for pets", Interdisciplinary Toxicology (2009)

dog.headline: Best kept away from dogs.
dog.summary: Eating an aloe plant can cause sudden, severe diarrhoea, sometimes with vomiting, and it can lower blood sugar. Keep the plant out of reach, and call your vet if your pet shows these signs.

cat.headline: Best kept away from cats.
cat.summary: Eating an aloe plant can cause sudden, severe diarrhoea, sometimes with vomiting, and it can lower blood sugar. Keep the plant out of reach, and call your vet if your pet shows these signs.

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Antidepressants such as fluoxetine or sertraline can make dogs drowsy, or the opposite: agitated, trembling, with a racing heart or a fever, and occasionally seizures. Most dogs recover well with prompt veterinary care, so call your vet if yours swallowed any.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Emergency — call your vet now.
dog.summary: Antifreeze tastes sweet, so dogs drink it readily, and it can be fatal. Within 30 minutes to 12 hours it causes signs like drunkenness — vomiting, wobbliness, drinking and urinating more — followed by kidney failure a few days later. Treatment works best the sooner it starts, so call your vet immediately, even if your dog seems fine.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Emergency — call your vet now.
cat.summary: Cats are even more sensitive to antifreeze than dogs, and kidney failure can follow within 12 to 24 hours. Its sweet taste makes it easy to swallow. Treatment works best the sooner it starts, so call your vet immediately, even if your cat seems fine.

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Dogs tolerate aspirin better than cats, but an overdose can still cause stomach ulcers, vomiting and fever. Only give it if your vet prescribed it, and call your vet if your dog swallowed tablets.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Cats are very sensitive to aspirin: their bodies take a very long time to clear it, so even amounts that would be fine for a dog can harm a cat. Call your vet straight away.

cat.headline: Best avoided for cats.

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Organophosphate insecticides — in some garden insecticides, fly baits and older flea products — cause drooling, vomiting, diarrhoea, twitching and breathing difficulty in dogs, and can progress to seizures and death. Signs usually start within minutes to hours. Call your vet now and bring the packaging.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Organophosphate insecticides — in some garden insecticides, fly baits and older flea products — cause drooling, vomiting, diarrhoea, twitching and breathing difficulty in cats, and can progress to seizures and death. Signs usually start within minutes to hours. Call your vet now and bring the packaging.

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Kalanchoe is one of the plants most often reported to cause serious, sometimes life-threatening, poisoning in dogs and cats. Early signs such as vomiting, drooling or tiredness don't show how serious it may become, so call your vet.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Kalanchoe is one of the plants most often reported to cause serious, sometimes life-threatening, poisoning in dogs and cats. Early signs such as vomiting, drooling or tiredness don't show how serious it may become, so call your vet.

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Lead — in old paint, fishing weights, lead shot, solder and some ceramic glazes — poisons dogs. It can cause loss of appetite, vomiting, diarrhoea, tiredness and behaviour changes, and in more serious cases wobbliness, tremors and seizures. Call your vet.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Lead — in old paint, fishing weights, lead shot, solder and some ceramic glazes — poisons cats. It can cause loss of appetite, vomiting, diarrhoea, tiredness and behaviour changes, and in more serious cases wobbliness, tremors and seizures. Call your vet.

dog.headline: Best kept away from dogs.
dog.summary: Lilies cause milder stomach upset in dogs than in cats — dogs are not known to develop the severe kidney failure cats do — but it's still worth keeping these plants out of reach and calling your vet if a dog eats a large amount.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: True lilies (Lilium species) and daylilies are severely toxic to cats — even a small bite of leaf or petal, a lick of pollen, or drinking vase water can cause fatal kidney failure. This is one of the most dangerous common houseplants for cats.

sources.label: Langston, "Acute renal failure caused by lily ingestion in six cats", J Am Vet Med Assoc (2002) — PubMed

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Lily of the valley affects the heart and can cause a dangerously irregular heartbeat, which can be fatal. Despite its name it isn't a true lily, and it's dangerous to dogs as well as cats. Call your vet straight away.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Lily of the valley affects the heart and can cause a dangerously irregular heartbeat, which can be fatal. Despite its name it isn't a true lily, and it's dangerous to dogs as well as cats. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Macadamia nuts cause a strange but usually short-lived syndrome in dogs — weakness, especially in the back legs, along with tremors and a raised temperature. The exact toxin isn't known, but the cases are well documented.

cat.headline: Not sure — no reported cases in cats, but ask your vet.
cat.summary: Macadamia toxicosis has only been documented in dogs; there isn't good evidence either way for cats, so treat any real ingestion as worth a call to your vet rather than assuming it's fine.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Macadamia Nut Toxicosis in Dogs

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Mistletoe can cause vomiting, severe diarrhoea, fast laboured breathing and shock, and can be fatal. Call your vet now.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Mistletoe can cause vomiting, severe diarrhoea, fast laboured breathing and shock, and can be fatal. Call your vet now.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Mothballs are toxic to all animals. They dissolve slowly, so they can keep causing harm after being eaten. Early signs are vomiting and loss of appetite; more serious poisoning can damage the blood and cause tremors or seizures. Call your vet.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Cats are thought to be more sensitive to mothballs than other animals. They dissolve slowly, so they can keep causing harm after being eaten, and serious poisoning can damage the blood and cause tremors or seizures. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicosis From Mothballs in Animals

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Naproxen stays in a dog's body for a long time, so its effects last. It can cause vomiting, stomach bleeding, pale gums and weakness. Only give it if your vet prescribed it, and call your vet if your dog swallowed any.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Cats may be even more sensitive to naproxen than dogs. It can cause vomiting, stomach bleeding and weakness. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicoses From Human Analgesics in Animals
FDA — Get the Facts about Pain Relievers for Pets

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Nicotine — in cigarettes, tobacco, nicotine patches and gum — most often causes vomiting, tiredness and brief agitation in dogs. Larger amounts can cause tremors, seizures, breathing difficulty and a slow heartbeat. Severe poisoning is uncommon but possible, so call your vet.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Nicotine — in cigarettes, tobacco, nicotine patches and gum — most often causes vomiting, tiredness and brief agitation in cats. Larger amounts can cause tremors, seizures, breathing difficulty and a slow heartbeat. Severe poisoning is uncommon but possible, so call your vet.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicosis in Animals From Human Topical Agents

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Oleander is one of the most toxic common garden plants. It affects the heart, causing an abnormal heartbeat, and deaths have been reported even with treatment. Call your vet straight away.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Oleander is one of the most toxic common garden plants, for cats as well as dogs. It affects the heart, causing an abnormal heartbeat, and deaths have been reported even with treatment. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Paracetamol can damage a dog's liver and blood. Dogs are less sensitive to it than cats, but only give it if your vet prescribed it, and call your vet if your dog swallowed tablets.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Paracetamol is fatal to cats: they can't break it down, and even a small amount is dangerous. Signs can appear within a few hours. Never give it to a cat, and call your vet immediately if your cat swallowed any, even if it seems fine.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicoses From Human Analgesics in Animals
FDA — Get the Facts about Pain Relievers for Pets

dog.headline: Best kept away from dogs.
dog.summary: Peace lily contains crystals that cause immediate pain, burning and swelling in the mouth, with drooling. Serious poisoning is rare, but call your vet if your dog has trouble breathing or swallowing.

cat.headline: Best kept away from cats.
cat.summary: Peace lily contains crystals that cause immediate pain, burning and swelling in the mouth, with drooling. Serious poisoning is rare, but call your vet if your cat has trouble breathing or swallowing.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals

dog.headline: Check the label before sharing.
dog.summary: Plain smooth peanut butter is on a university veterinary hospital's list of treats, but some peanut butters are sweetened with xylitol, which is dangerous to dogs. Check the label: if it lists xylitol or birch sugar, treat it as xylitol poisoning and call your vet.

cat.headline: Not sure — ask your vet.
cat.summary: One university veterinary list includes plain peanut butter as a treat for cats, which isn't enough for us to give you an answer. Xylitol, the sweetener that makes some peanut butters dangerous to dogs, doesn't seem to be as dangerous for cats. Ask your vet if you're unsure.

sources.label: NC State Veterinary Hospital — Healthy Human Food Treats For Pets
Merck Veterinary Manual — Xylitol Toxicosis in Dogs

dog.headline: Not sure — ask your vet.
dog.summary: Our sources describe how dangerous these products are to cats, but don't cover a dog licking or swallowing them. If that happened, call your vet and have the packaging to hand.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Many flea and tick treatments made for dogs contain permethrin or similar insecticides, which can be deadly to cats. Never use a dog product on a cat. Signs include drooling, vomiting, twitching and seizures. Call your vet immediately.

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: A warm stomach is an ideal place for raw yeast dough to keep rising, stretching the stomach, and the yeast produces alcohol as it ferments — so a dog gets both a mechanical problem and alcohol poisoning from the same mouthful.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Any animal can be affected by raw yeast dough: it keeps rising in the warm stomach, and the fermenting yeast produces alcohol. If your cat ate some, call your vet.

cat.headline: Not sure — ask your vet.

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Emergency — call your vet now.
dog.summary: Rat and mouse baits use different poisons. Some cause internal bleeding that only shows 3 to 7 days later; others cause seizures or kidney damage. Treat any ingestion as an emergency, even if your dog seems fine, and bring the packaging so your vet knows which poison it is.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Emergency — call your vet now.
cat.summary: Cats can be poisoned by eating bait, or by eating a rodent that ate it. Rat and mouse baits use different poisons: some cause internal bleeding days later, others seizures or kidney damage. Call your vet now and bring the packaging.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Anticoagulant Rodenticide Poisoning in Animals
Cornell Feline Health Center — Poisons
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Dogs are extremely sensitive to sago palms (cycads). Eating one can cause severe vomiting and diarrhoea, followed by liver failure. The first signs often appear within a few hours and liver damage can follow over the next two to three days, so call your vet straight away, even if your dog seems fine.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Sago palm is one of the plants reported to cause life-threatening poisoning in cats as well as dogs. Early signs such as vomiting or drooling don't show how serious it is, and liver damage can appear a day or two later. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
Milewski & Khan, "An overview of potentially life-threatening poisonous plants in dogs and cats", J Vet Emerg Crit Care (2006)

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Homemade play dough, salt dough and rock salt contain a lot of salt, and eating them can cause salt poisoning. Vomiting usually starts within a few hours and can progress to tremors and seizures, which can be fatal. Call your vet straight away.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Homemade play dough, salt dough and rock salt contain a lot of salt, and eating them can cause salt poisoning, which can be fatal. Call your vet straight away.

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Most slug and snail baits contain metaldehyde. It causes severe tremors, a dangerously high body temperature and seizures, starting from 30 minutes to a few hours after eating it. It can be life-threatening but responds well to prompt treatment. Call your vet immediately and bring the packaging.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Most slug and snail baits contain metaldehyde, which causes muscle spasms, wobbliness and seizures in cats. It can be life-threatening but responds well to prompt treatment. Call your vet immediately and bring the packaging.

dog.summary: Vitamin D supplements can raise blood calcium to dangerous levels and cause kidney failure, which can be fatal. Vomiting, tiredness, and increased thirst and urination usually start 12 to 48 hours after eating them. Call your vet even if your pet seems fine.

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Wild mushrooms are hard to identify, even for experts, and some, like the death cap, are deadly: a single mushroom can kill a dog. The most dangerous kinds often cause no signs for 6 to 24 hours, then attack the liver and kidneys. Don't wait for signs: call your vet now.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Wild mushrooms are hard to identify, even for experts, and some, like the death cap, are deadly: a single mushroom can kill a cat. The most dangerous kinds often cause no signs for 6 to 24 hours, then attack the liver and kidneys. Don't wait for signs: call your vet now.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Overview of Mushrooms Toxic to Animals
"Case Report: α-amanitin toxicosis leading to acute death in a puppy", Front Vet Sci (2025)

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Xylitol, a sweetener in many sugar-free gums, sweets, mints and baked goods and in some peanut butters, causes a sudden, dangerous drop in blood sugar in dogs and can damage the liver. Signs can start within 30 minutes. Always check the label.

cat.headline: Not sure — cats aren't known to be affected the same way, but ask your vet.
cat.summary: Xylitol poisoning has only been reported in dogs, and cats don't seem to be at the same risk. That still isn't enough for us to give you an answer for cats, so ask your vet if you're unsure.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Xylitol Toxicosis in Dogs

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Yew is extremely poisonous. It can stop the heart, and once signs appear, treatment often can't help. If your pet has chewed any part of a yew, call your vet immediately, before any signs appear.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Yew is extremely poisonous. It can stop the heart, and once signs appear, treatment often can't help. If your pet has chewed any part of a yew, call your vet immediately, before any signs appear.

dog.summary: US pennies minted after 1982 are mostly zinc. Swallowed, they can release zinc that destroys red blood cells and damages the kidneys, which can be fatal. Call your vet: a coin may need to be removed.
